Once upon a time, there was a girl called Poppy. Poppy was only three years old and she was out for a walk in the park. 
Suddenly, Poppy saw a buckle on the ground. It was a really pretty buckle, but it was also very dirty.
Poppy wanted to pick up the buckle, so she bent down and pinch it. Then she saw a strange thing - the buckle began to move. 
It wasn’t a buckle at all - it was a tiny little mouse!
The mouse said to Poppy: “Oh help me! I am stuck inside this buckle and I cannot get out!”
Poppy was not scared, so she bent down and carefully opened the buckle. Then the little mouse thanked her and scurried away.
Poppy smiled and put the buckle in her pocket. She was happy she could help the little mouse.

One day, a little dog named Spot found a big, soft toy. He wanted to play with it, but it was stuck in a box. Spot tried to open the box. He pushed and pulled, but the box did not open.
Spot saw his friend, Cat. He asked, "Cat, can you help me open the box?" Cat came over and used her claws to snap the box open. The soft toy was free. Spot was happy and said, "Thank you, Cat!"
Spot and Cat played with the soft toy together. They had lots of fun. The moral of the story is that if we help each other, we can do things that are hard to do alone.

On his way back home, George saw a lost puppy. He felt so sorry for the puppy. Without thinking further, he scooped it in his arms and brought the puppy back home. 
George decided to take care of the puppy. He fed the puppy and named him Rover.
George took the telephone to call his friends and asked them, "Can you help me find a home for Rover?"
His friends said, "Yes, of course! We will help you look for a home for Rover."
George was so glad that he had found such kind friends and he hugged Rover tightly. From then on, George took good care of Rover and always made sure he had plenty to eat. 
George was very happy and thankful that he had found a friend who he could rely on.

Lily is surprised. She feels her cheek get warm. She looks at Ben and sees him blush.
Miss Rose is surprised too. She laughs and snaps the picture.
"Ben, why did you kiss Lily?" Miss Rose asks.
"Because I like her. She is my friend." Ben says.
"That's very sweet, Ben. But you should always ask before you kiss someone. Do you understand?" Miss Rose says.
"Yes, Miss Rose. I'm sorry, Lily. Can I kiss you?" Ben says.
Lily thinks for a moment. She likes Ben too. He is her friend. She nods and smiles.
"Okay, Ben. You can kiss me." Lily says.
They kiss again, gently and quickly. They giggle and hug.
Miss Rose smiles and shows them the picture. It is a nice picture. They see their house, their kiss, and their happy faces.
They like the picture. They like their house. They like each other. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear. He was walking in the woods when he saw something strange - a TV! He had never seen one before and was curious to know more. He went up to the TV, but was startled when he heard a voice come from it.
"What are you doing here?" the voice asked.
The bear was so afraid he froze in place. Finally he said, "I just wanted to see what this was?"
The voice then replied, "This is mine, and you can't have it. Now go away."
The bear didn't want to leave empty handed, so he said, "If I can't have the TV, then can I at least bury it?"
The voice thought for a moment and replied, "That's a good idea. You can have the TV if you bury it deep in the ground."
So the bear dug a hole, put the TV in and covered it up. He was so clumsy he had to try a few times before he got it all buried. When he finished, he felt proud that he had buried the TV so deep.
The end.

"Yes, Ben, they are so pretty and fun!" Lila said. "But we should share them with other kids too. Maybe someone left them here for us to share."
But Ben did not want to share. He wanted to keep all the toys for himself. He started to grab the toys and put them in his bag. He grabbed a doll, a car, a ball, a book, and more.
"Ben, stop!" Lila said. "You are grabbing too many toys! Leave some for me and for other kids!"
"No, Lila, they are mine!" Ben said. "I found them first! You can't have any!"
Lila was sad and angry. She tried to grab some toys back, but Ben pushed her away. He was very mean and greedy.
Then, they heard a loud voice. It was the owner of the toys. He was a big boy who had left the box under the tree for a while. He saw Ben and Lila fighting over his toys.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing with my toys?" he shouted. "Give them back to me right now!"
He ran to the box and grabbed his toys from Ben's bag. He was very mad and strong. He also grabbed Ben and Lila by their arms and dragged them to their parents.
He told their parents what they had done. Their parents were very disappointed and angry. They scolded Ben and Lila and made them apologize to the big boy. They also took away their own toys for a week.
Ben and Lila felt very sorry and ashamed. They learned a hard lesson. They learned that they should not grab things that are not theirs. They learned that they should share and be humble. They learned that being greedy and mean can lead to trouble and pain.

The mouse could not resist his curiosity and touched the hot pot. He felt a lot of pain and cried out loud. The cat came running and said, "I told you not to touch it." The mouse learned that he should listen to others and not touch unknown things. But his paw hurt a lot, and he was sad.

Anna likes to jump. She jumps on her bed, on the sofa, on the grass. She jumps with her friends, with her dog, with her doll. She jumps when she is happy, when she is bored, when she is angry.
One day, Anna finds a pretty diary in her mom's room. It has a pink cover and a lock. Anna wants to see what is inside. She jumps on the bed and reaches for the diary. She tries to open it, but it is locked. She looks for the key, but she cannot find it.
She hears her mom coming. She jumps off the bed and hides the diary under her pillow. She pretends to read a book.
"Hi, Anna. What are you doing?" her mom asks.
"Reading," Anna says.
"Can I see your book?" her mom asks.
Anna gives her the book. Her mom smiles and sits on the bed. She feels something under the pillow. She lifts it and sees the diary.
"Anna, what is this?" her mom asks.
Anna feels scared. She jumps off the bed and runs to the door.
"Sorry, mom. I just wanted to see it. It is so pretty. Please don't be mad," Anna says.
Her mom sighs and calls her back. She hugs her and says, "Anna, this is my diary. It is very special to me. It has all my secrets and memories. I don't like it when you take my things without asking. Do you understand?"
Anna nods and says, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I won't do it again."
Her mom smiles and says, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will never jump on the bed again. It is dangerous. You could fall and hurt yourself. Do you promise?"
Anna thinks for a moment. She likes to jump on the bed. But she loves her mom more. She says, "Yes, mom. I promise. I will never jump on the bed again."
Her mom kisses her and says, "Good girl. I love you, Anna."
"I love you, too, mom," Anna says.
They hug and laugh. Anna is happy. She doesn't need the diary. She has her mom. And she can still jump on other things.

Ben was troubled. He wanted to know what the wolf did and why it was scary. He waited until his mom was busy in the kitchen and then he stretched his arm to reach the book. He pulled it down and opened it. He could not read the words, but he saw more pictures of the wolf. The wolf was chasing a girl in a red hood, a boy in a straw house, and three pigs in a brick house. The wolf looked angry and hungry.
Ben felt afraid. He wished he had listened to his mom and left the book alone. He wanted to close it and put it back, but he was too scared to touch it. He started to cry and call for his mom. His mom heard him and came to see what was wrong. She saw the book and the tears on his face. She was angry and sad.
She took the book from him and put it away. She scolded him for being naughty and disobedient. She said he could not listen to any stories for a week. She sent him to his room without a hug or a kiss. Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he could say sorry and hug his mom. He wished he could stretch his arms and legs and feel big and strong again. But he could not. He lay on his bed and sobbed. He had a bad day.

He said, "It's so easy to skip...just try one and see. The sky will be so happy with us!" Together they skipped around the rock, and soon their faces were beaming with joy. Jill remembered the lesson and said, "Friendship makes everything easy."
The moral of this story is that with a friend by your side, anything is possible. Friendship makes it easier to do anything, even the things that seem scary!

Lily liked to play with bugs. She liked to catch them and look at them. She liked their colors and shapes. She liked how they moved and made noises. She had a jar with holes for her bugs.
One day, she found a pretty cricket. It was green and shiny. It had long legs and wings. It made a loud chirp. Lily wanted to keep it. She put it in her jar with some grass and water.
But the cricket did not like the jar. It wanted to be free. It wanted to hop and fly. It wanted to find other crickets. It tried to get out. It pushed and kicked. It bit and scratched. It made a lot of noise.
Lily did not like the noise. She wanted the cricket to be quiet. She wanted it to be happy. She thought it was hungry. She gave it some bread and cheese. But the cricket did not want bread and cheese. It wanted grass and seeds. It spit out the food. It made more noise.
Lily got angry. She grabbed the jar. She shook it hard. She yelled at the cricket. She said, "Be quiet! Be good! Or I will hurt you!" But the cricket did not listen. It kept chirping and fighting. It did not care about Lily.
Lily got a sharp stick. She opened the jar. She poked the cricket. She wanted to make it stop. But the cricket did not stop. It jumped at Lily. It bit her finger. It made her bleed. It made her cry.
Lily dropped the jar. She ran away. She left the cricket. The cricket was free. It hopped and flew. It found other crickets. It was happy. But Lily was not happy. She was hurt and sad. She lost her pretty cricket. She learned a hard lesson.

"It's okay, Lily. I know you were having fun. But sometimes you have to be careful and follow the rules. They are there to keep you safe." Daddy said, wiping her tears.

"I love you too, Lily." Daddy said, kissing her. "You are still my impressive little girl."

After mom left, Tim and Kim decided to play with the mattress. They dragged it to the middle of the room and started to jump on it. They had fun bouncing and laughing and making silly faces. But then, Tim had an idea.
"Let's make the mattress more fun," he said. "Let's put some juice on it and make it slippery."
Kim thought that was a bad idea. She said, "No, Tim, that's dangerous. We could fall and hurt ourselves. And we could spoil the mattress and make mom angry."
But Tim did not listen. He grabbed a bottle of juice and poured some on the mattress. He said, "Come on, Kim, don't be a baby. It's just juice. It will dry up."
He jumped on the mattress and slid on the juice. He said, "Whee, this is fun. Try it, Kim."
Kim shook her head. She said, "No, Tim, I don't want to. It's not fun, it's stupid. Stop it, Tim, or I'll tell mom."
But Tim did not stop. He poured more juice on the mattress and jumped and slid. He said, "You're no fun, Kim. You're a boring girl. I'm having a blast."
He did not see that the juice was dripping on the floor and making a big puddle. He did not hear that mom was coming back and opening the door. He did not notice that mom was shocked and angry when she saw the mess.
"Tim, Kim, what have you done?" mom yelled. "You spoiled the mattress and the floor. You made a huge mess. You were very naughty and dangerous. How could you do this?"
Tim and Kim stopped jumping and looked at mom. They felt scared and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were just playing. We didn't mean to spoil the mattress."
Mom sighed. She said, "Playing is good, but you have to be careful and respectful. You have to listen to each other and to me. You have to clean up your mess and apologize. And you have to promise me you will never do this again."
Tim and Kim nodded. They said, "We promise, mom. We're sorry, mom. We love you, mom."
Mom hugged them. She said, "I love you too, Tim and Kim. But you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's get some towels and clean this up. And then, you have to go to bed early. No more playing with the mattress today."

"Sorry, I didn't see it," the boy said, and rode away.

"A boy on a bike spilled it. He was careless," Ben said.
"Oh no, that's not fair. I'm thirsty," Anna said.
"Me too," Ben said.
They looked at their mom, who was sitting on a bench. She saw their faces and smiled.
"Don't worry, I have another bottle in my bag. Come here, and I'll give you some," she said.
Anna and Ben ran to their mom and hugged her. She gave them the bottle and they drank some juice. They thanked her and felt better.
They learned to be more careful with their things and to watch out for careless people. They also learned that their mom always had a backup plan. They continued to play and have fun in the park.

One day, Momo saw a very big banana high up in the tree. He wanted to eat it, but he could not reach it. Momo asked his friend, the bird, "Can you help me get the banana?" The bird said, "Yes, I can help you." So, the bird flew up and tried to get the banana for Momo.
But, when the bird touched the banana, something unexpected happened. The big banana fell from the tree and broke into many little bananas. Momo and the bird were very surprised. They called all their friends, and everyone ate the little bananas together. It was a fun day for Momo and his friends.

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But one day, the park was closed. There was a big sign that said "No Entry". Sara and Tom were sad.
"Why is the park closed?" Sara asked.
"Maybe they are fixing something," Tom said.
"Or maybe they are making something new," Sara said.
They decided to walk around the fence and see if they could find out. They saw some men with big machines and tools. They were digging and building and painting. Sara and Tom were curious.
"What are they doing?" Tom asked.
"Let's go closer and see," Sara said.
They sneaked behind a tree and peeked at the men. They saw something shiny and round and tall. It looked like a big flower. Sara and Tom gasped.
"Wow, what is that?" Sara asked.
"It looks like a giant sunflower," Tom said.
"Maybe it can grow and grow and touch the sky," Sara said.
They wanted to touch it and climb it and play with it. They forgot about the sign and the fence and the men. They ran towards the big flower. But before they could reach it, they heard a loud voice.
"Hey, you kids, get away from there!" the voice shouted.
It was one of the men. He saw Sara and Tom and ran after them. He looked angry and scary. Sara and Tom were scared.
"Run, run!" Tom said.
They turned around and ran as fast as they could. They ran back to the fence and jumped over it. They ran all the way home. They were out of breath and out of fun.
"That was not fun," Sara said.
"That was dull," Tom said.
They wished the park would open again soon. They missed the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They did not want to see the big flower again. They learned their lesson. They would not sneak around the fence again. They would wait until the park was ready. Maybe then, they would have fun again.

One day, Lisa and her Daddy went to the store. Daddy had to get some items for their house. He took something off the shelf and looked it over.
Lisa asked, "What is it, Daddy?"
He smiled. "It's a doorbell. When we get home, we can put it up."
Lisa was very excited. She ran to the cash register and waited impatiently. 
Suddenly, the doorbell rang. Lisa was surprised. The doorbell was ringing even though it wasn't in the house yet.
"Why is it ringing, Daddy?"
"That must mean someone is here," he said. He opened the door, and there was Lisa's friend, Bill. He was holding a note.
"Hi Bill!" said Lisa.
Bill handed the note to Daddy, who thanked him and opened it. Inside was a message from Lisa's Mommy. With a smile, Daddy handed the note to Lisa.
"Your Mommy wants you to come home right away."
Lisa nodded and smiled. She was eager to get home to see what their new doorbell looked like.

Timmy was a little mouse who liked to drink milk. He lived in a big house with his family and many other mice. Sometimes, he would sneak into the kitchen at night and look for a bowl of milk to drink.
One night, he found a bowl of milk on the table. He climbed up a chair and reached for the bowl. He smelled the milk and it was delicious. He licked his lips and started to drink.
"Hello, little mouse," said a voice behind him. Timmy turned around and saw a big cat. The cat had yellow eyes and sharp teeth. He looked hungry and angry. Timmy was scared and wanted to run away.
"Please don't eat me, Mr. Cat," Timmy said. "I just wanted some milk. It was delicious."
"Well, I want some milk too," the cat said. "And I want some mouse. You look delicious."
The cat jumped on the table and chased Timmy. Timmy ran as fast as he could. He dodged the cat's paws and ran to the edge of the table. He saw a window and jumped out. He landed on a tree branch and climbed down.
He ran back to his family and told them what happened. They hugged him and said he was brave. They gave him some cheese and water. Timmy was happy and safe. He learned a lesson. He decided not to drink milk from the table again. He drank water from the sink instead. It was not as delicious, but it was safer.

Mia was an adventurous girl. She liked to explore new places and find new things. One day, she saw a big hole in the ground. She wondered what was inside. She decided to go in and have a look.
She crawled into the hole. It was dark and damp. She felt something soft and furry. She said, "Hello, who are you?"
A voice said, "I am a mole. This is my home. Who are you?"
Mia said, "I am Mia. I am a girl. I like to explore. Can I see your home?"
The mole said, "No, you can't. You are too big. You don't fit in here. You are making a mess. You are scaring my family. You have to go out."
Mia said, "But I want to see more. I want to be your friend. Please let me stay."
The mole said, "No, you can't. You are not a mole. You are a girl. You belong outside. Go out now."
Mia felt sad and angry. She did not want to go out. She wanted to see more. She tried to crawl deeper into the hole. But she got stuck. She could not move. She started to cry.
The mole heard her cry. He felt sorry for her. He said, "Don't cry, Mia. I will help you. I will dig you out. But you have to promise me something."
Mia said, "What do I have to promise?"
The mole said, "You have to promise me that you will not come into my home again. You have to respect my space. You have to find your own place to explore. Do you promise?"
Mia said, "Yes, I promise. I am sorry, mole. I did not mean to bother you. I just wanted to see your home. But I understand that it is not for me. Thank you for helping me."
The mole said, "You are welcome, Mia. I am sorry, too. I was rude to you. I just wanted to protect my home. But I understand that you are curious. Thank you for promising me."
The mole dug Mia out of the hole. Mia crawled out. She saw the sun and the sky. She felt happy and free. She said, "Goodbye, mole. I hope you have a good day. Maybe we can see each other again. But not in your home. In another place."
The mole said, "Goodbye, Mia. I hope you have a good day, too. Maybe we can see each other again. But not in my home. In another place."

"NO, TIM, NO!" Mia screams, as she sees her doll get hurt. She picks up her doll and hugs her. "You are bad. You broke my doll. I hate you!"

"Okay, Mia. I will be gentle. And I will be quiet." Tim says, as he walks to Mia and her doll. "Maybe we can find some glue and some tape. And maybe we can find a new dress. And maybe we can comb her hair. And maybe we can make her happy again."
Mia and Tim work together to fix the doll. They find some glue and some tape. They find a new dress. They comb her hair. They make her happy again.

Once upon a time, there were two brave adventurers named Lucy and Jack. They were exploring a dark, dangerous cave. Suddenly, Jack saw a bone lying on the ground. "Look Lucy! I found a bone. What should we do?" 
Lucy thought for a moment and then smiled. "Hold onto it! It could come in handy." 
Jack picked up the bone but it glowed with a bright light. He felt scared but they kept exploring.
Finally, they reached the end of the cave. Lucy looked around and then saw a giant monster. Its stomping shook the cave and Jack gulped.
But then Lucy started to display the bone. Suddenly, the monster stopped moving. Its eyes widened, and it stepped aside.
Jack could hardly believe it. He looked at Lucy and said, "Thanks for having the brilliant idea of displaying the bone! I thought it was dangerous but it saved us!" 
Lucy smiled and said, "I knew it would work! Let's get out of this cave!" 
So, with courage and bravery, Lucy and Jack safely made it out of the dangerous cave.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a tall trunk. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds.
"Come on, Lily, let's go up!" Tom said.
"OK, Tom, but be careful!" Lily said.
They climbed the tree and reached a branch. They saw a nest with three eggs. They were blue and speckled.
"Wow, look at the eggs!" Tom said. "They are so pretty!"
"Yes, they are!" Lily said. "But we should not touch them. They belong to the birds."
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It came to the park and stopped near the tree. A man got out of the truck. He had a saw and a rope.
"What is he doing?" Tom asked.
"I don't know, but it looks bad!" Lily said.
The man started to cut the tree with the saw. The tree shook and the branch cracked.
"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily shouted.
The man did not hear them. He kept cutting the tree. The branch broke and Tom and Lily fell.
But they did not hit the ground. They landed on something soft and furry. It was a bear. The bear had seen the man and the truck. He had run to the park to rescue the tree and the birds. He had caught Tom and Lily with his back.
"Thank you, bear!" Tom and Lily said.
The bear nodded and growled. He carried them to a safe place. He put them down and licked their faces.
"You are welcome, kids!" the bear said. "But you should not climb trees that are in danger. It is not safe."
"We are sorry, bear!" Tom and Lily said. "We did not know. We just wanted to see the birds."
The bear smiled and hugged them. He showed them the way back to their parents. He waved goodbye and went back to the forest.
Tom and Lily ran to their parents and told them what happened. Their parents were scared and happy. They thanked the bear and the park ranger who had stopped the man and the truck. They learned that the tree and the birds were protected and that the man was a bad guy who wanted to cut them down. They were glad that the bear had rescued them and the tree. They promised to never climb trees that were in danger again. They also promised to be friends with the bear and the birds. They went home and drew pictures of their adventure. They had a lot of fun.

Lily followed the woman to Ben's room. She saw a boy with brown hair and blue eyes, sitting on the floor with a train set. He looked up and saw Lily and his mom.
The woman said, "Ben, this is Lily. She lives on our street. She made you a picture of our house and our family. Isn't that nice?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. I like trains. Can I see yours?"
Ben said, "Sure, come on. I have a lot of them. You can be the conductor."

Sam and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to pretend they were driving on the road and going to different places. Sam had a blue car and Lily had a pink car.
"Beep beep! Move out of the way, Lily!" Sam said as he zoomed his car past Lily's car.
"Hey, that's not fair, Sam! You bumped into my car!" Lily said as she chased after Sam's car.
They both drove their cars around the sofa, the table, and the chair, making loud noises and laughing. But then, they saw Mom coming into the room with a frown on her face.
"Sam and Lily, what are you doing? You are making too much noise and mess! You need to settle down and play quietly. And where are your licenses?" Mom asked.
"Licenses?" Sam and Lily said together, looking confused.
"Yes, licenses. You need a license to drive a car, even a toy car. It's a card that shows you know how to drive safely and follow the rules. Do you have your licenses?" Mom asked.
Sam and Lily shook their heads. They didn't have any licenses. They didn't even know what they were.
"Then you can't drive your cars anymore. You have to put them away and find something else to play with. Maybe you can draw some licenses and practice driving on paper. But first, you have to say sorry to each other for bumping and shouting." Mom said.
Sam and Lily looked at each other and felt sorry. They didn't mean to upset Mom or each other. They put their cars away and hugged each other.
"Sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to bump into your car." Sam said.
"Sorry, Sam. I didn't mean to chase after your car." Lily said.
"It's okay. We can still be friends and play together." Sam said.
"Okay. Let's go and draw some licenses and learn how to drive better." Lily said.
They took some paper and crayons and went to the table. They drew some cards with their names and pictures of their cars. They showed them to Mom and asked her to teach them some rules of driving. Mom smiled and helped them. They learned how to stop, go, turn, and share the road. They had fun and played quietly. They were good drivers and good children.

"Bye, robot," they said. "We will play with you again tomorrow."

But Sara did not listen to him. She pulled his reins, and said, "Come on, Spot, let's go! I want to ride you to the pond, and see the ducks!"
Spot tried to tell Sara that he was sleepy, and that he needed a break. He neighed softly, and shook his head. He looked at his stable, and hoped Sara would understand. But Sara did not understand. She thought Spot was being stubborn, and she got angry. She kicked his sides, and said, "Move, Spot, move! You are a bad pony, and you don't love me!"
Spot felt hurt by Sara's words, and he felt a bitter taste in his mouth. He did not want to fight with Sara, but he also did not want to go to the pond. He was too tired, and he knew he would fall down if he ran too fast. He decided to do something he had never done before. He bucked, and threw Sara off his back.
Sara landed on the ground, and she cried out loud. She scraped her knee, and she felt a sharp pain. She looked at Spot, and she saw him run away to his stable. She felt scared, and sorry. She realized that she had been mean to Spot, and that she had not listened to him. She wished she had been nicer to him, and let him nap.
She got up, and limped to the stable. She saw Spot lying on the hay, and she heard him snore. She felt a tear roll down her cheek, and she whispered, "I'm sorry, Spot, I'm sorry. You are a good pony, and I love you. Please forgive me, and let me be your friend again."
Spot heard Sara's voice, and he opened his eyes. He saw her sad face, and he felt a warm feeling in his heart. He knew she was sorry, and he forgave her. He lifted his head, and nuzzled her hand. He said, "It's okay, Sara, it's okay. I'm sorry too, and I love you. You are my friend, and I'm glad you came to see me."
Sara smiled, and hugged Spot's neck. She said, "Thank you, Spot, thank you. You are my friend, and I'm happy you are here. Can I stay with you, and nap with you?"
Spot nodded, and said, "Yes, Sara, yes. You can stay with me, and nap with me. We can go to the pond later, and see the ducks. But first, let's rest, and dream."
Sara and Spot lay down on the hay, and closed their eyes. They snuggled together, and felt peaceful. They learned a lesson that day, and they never forgot it. They learned to listen to each other, and to be kind. They learned that napping is good, and that bitter words are bad. They learned that friendship is precious, and that love is sweet.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" she said.
Her mom heard her and came to see what was wrong. She saw the blood on Sara's finger and the needle on the floor.
"Oh, Sara, what happened?" she asked.
"I was making a doll and the needle poked me," Sara said.
Her mom hugged her and took her to the bathroom. She washed her finger and put a band-aid on it.
"There, there, it's okay. The needle won't hurt you anymore," she said.
"Thank you, mom. I'm sorry I was loud," Sara said.
"It's okay, honey. I know you were just trying to have fun. But you have to be careful with needles. They are not toys. They are tools for grown-ups," her mom said.
"I understand, mom. Can I still make my doll?" Sara asked.
"Of course you can. But let me help you. I'll show you how to use the needle safely. And maybe we can find some other things to fill your doll with. How about some beans or rice?" her mom said.
"Okay, mom. That sounds good. Can we make a doll for you too?" Sara said.
"Sure, why not? I would love a doll from you. Then we can both have a friend to play with," her mom said.
Sara smiled. She was not lonely anymore. She had her mom and her dolls. She was happy.

The bees came out of the tree and chased Bobby. Bobby tried to run away, but the bees were very fast. He cried, "I just wanted some honey! Please don't be mad!" But the bees did not stop. They stung Bobby, and it hurt a lot.
Bobby learned that taking honey without asking is not nice. He was very sad and his face was all red from the bee stings. The bad ending made Bobby remember to always ask before taking something that is not his.

Ben and Lily were playing on the beach. They liked to build sand castles and dig holes. They also liked to watch the water go in and out. They knew it was called the tide.
"Look, Lily, the tide is going out!" Ben said. "We can go closer to the water and find shells and crabs."
"OK, Ben, but we have to be careful. Mom said not to go too far. The tide can change and come back fast." Lily said.
They ran to the water and started to look for treasures. They found some shiny shells and some funny crabs. They put them in their buckets. They were having fun.
But they did not notice that the tide was starting to reverse. The water was coming back in. It was getting closer and closer to their sand castles and holes.
"Ben, Lily, come back!" Mom shouted. "The tide is reversing! It's important to stay safe!"
Ben and Lily heard Mom and looked at the water. It was very near their sand castles and holes. They were scared.
"Quick, Lily, grab your bucket and run!" Ben said.
They ran back to Mom with their buckets. They were sad to leave their sand castles and holes, but they were glad to be safe.
"Good job, Ben and Lily. You listened to me and came back. The tide can be dangerous sometimes. It's important to pay attention to it." Mom said.
She hugged them and gave them a snack. They ate their snack and looked at their shells and crabs. They were happy. They learned something new about the tide.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big ladder leaning on the wall. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the roof.
"Let's go up the ladder!" Ben said.
"OK, but be careful!" Lily said.
They ran to the ladder and started to climb. Ben went first and Lily followed. They were almost at the top when they heard a loud crack.
"Oh no! The ladder is broken!" Ben shouted.
He looked down and saw that one of the steps had snapped. He was scared and held on tight.
"Lily, don't move! The ladder is broken!" he repeated.
Lily heard him and stopped. She was scared too. She looked down and saw how high they were.
"Ben, what do we do?" she asked.
"Help! Help! We need help!" Ben yelled.
He hoped that someone would hear them and come to help. He wished they had not climbed the ladder. It was a bad idea.
Soon, they heard a voice.
"Ben! Lily! What are you doing up there?" It was their dad. He had come home from work and saw them on the roof.
"Dad! Dad! The ladder is broken! We are stuck!" Ben cried.
"Don't worry, I'm coming!" their dad said.
He ran to the ladder and saw the broken step. He was angry and worried. He told them to stay calm and not to move. He climbed up the ladder carefully and reached them. He hugged them and said.
"Are you OK? You are very lucky you didn't fall. You could have been hurt. Why did you climb the ladder? It was dangerous!"
"Sorry, dad. We wanted to see the roof. We didn't know the ladder was broken." Ben said.
"Sorry, dad. We were curious. We won't do it again." Lily said.
Their dad shook his head and said.
"Come on, let's go down. I'll fix the ladder later. And you two, no more climbing ladders. Promise?"
"Promise, dad." Ben and Lily said.
They went down the ladder with their dad. They were glad they were safe. They learned their lesson. They never climbed ladders again.

Mom takes out a big pot and fills it with water. She puts it on the stove and turns it on. Then she takes out some carrots, potatoes, celery and an onion. She peels and chops them and puts them in a bowl. Sara watches and wants to help.
Mom gives Sara a small knife and a purple onion. She says, "Be careful, this onion can make your eyes water. But it will make the soup very yummy." Sara nods and tries to cut the onion like mom. But as soon as she slices it, she feels a sting in her eyes. She rubs them and starts to cry.
Mom sees Sara crying and hugs her. She says, "Oh, poor Sara. The onion is too strong for you. Here, let me show you a trick." She takes Sara to the sink and turns on the cold water. She tells Sara to splash some water on her face and eyes. Sara does as mom says and feels better.
Mom says, "See, the water helps to wash away the onion juice. Now you can smile again." Sara smiles and hugs mom. She says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. Can I still help you with the soup?" Mom says, "Of course, you can. You are my little helper. Come on, let's finish the soup and have some fun." Sara and mom go back to the kitchen and finish the soup. They have a delicious lunch and a happy day.

The trees replied, "It must be a secret!"
So Bob kept walking, trying to figure out what the secret was. He asked the birds and the bees but they just chirped and hummed and wouldn't tell him anything.
Finally Bob asked an owl, "What is the secret?"
The wise owl hooted, "Eat less food and you will be less fat, this is your sneezing secret!" 
Bob was so happy he had learned the secret that he ran home and started eating less food. He was soon no longer fat and he was never sneezing again.

"Or a bridge for the cars?" Tom asked.
"Or both?" Sara and Tom said together.
They liked the idea. They thanked Mom and went to work. They used the hanger and some string and some tape. They made a swing and a bridge. They played with their dolls and cars. They were happy.

But then, Jack throws the ball too hard. It flies over the fence and lands in the street. Jill and Jack run to the fence and look for the ball. They see a car coming. The car is fast and loud and scary.
"Look out, ball!" Jill shouts.
The car hits the ball. The ball pops and makes a loud noise. The car stops and the driver gets out. He is angry and says bad words.
"Hey, you kids! What are you doing? This is my ball! You broke it!" he yells.
Jill and Jack are scared and sad. They did not know the ball was his. They did not mean to break it. They say sorry to the driver.
The driver is still angry. He takes the ball and goes back to his car. He drives away and leaves Jill and Jack alone.
Jill and Jack go back to the yard. They do not want to play anymore. They sit under an ancient tree and hug each other.
"Maybe we can find another ball," Jack says.
"Maybe," Jill says.
They look at the sky and see a rainbow. It is bright and beautiful and makes them smile.
"Maybe the rainbow is a sign," Jill says.
"A sign of what?" Jack asks.
"A sign that everything will be okay," Jill says.
They hope she is right. They hold hands and watch the rainbow. They feel a little better.

Lily and Max were friends who liked to paint. They had many colors and brushes to make pretty pictures. One day, they found a big rock in the park. They decided to paint the rock together.
Lily wanted to paint the rock blue, like the sky. Max wanted to paint the rock green, like the grass. They argued and pulled the rock from each other. The rock was too heavy and it fell on the ground. It broke into two pieces.
"Oh no!" Lily cried. "We broke the rock! Now we can't paint it!"
"It's your fault!" Max shouted. "You wanted to paint it blue! Blue is a silly color for a rock!"
"No, it's your fault!" Lily yelled back. "You wanted to paint it green! Green is a boring color for a rock!"
They were so angry that they stopped being friends. They took their colors and brushes and went home.
The next day, they saw the rock again in the park. It was still broken, but someone had painted it. One piece was blue and the other piece was green. They also had flowers and stars and hearts on them. The rock looked very pretty.
Lily and Max felt sorry for breaking the rock and fighting with each other. They realized that they both had good ideas and that they could share and cooperate. They also saw a note next to the rock. It said:
"Dear Lily and Max,
I saw your rock and I liked it. I wanted to make it more beautiful for you. I hope you like it too. I think blue and green are both nice colors for a rock. They remind me of the earth. You are lucky to have each other as friends. Friends are more important than rocks.
Love,
Mom"
Lily and Max smiled and hugged each other. They thanked their mom for painting the rock and for teaching them a lesson. They learned that they should respect each other's opinions and that they should not fight over small things. They also learned that their mom loved them very much and that she was very clever and kind. They decided to paint more rocks together and to give them to their mom as a gift.

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood. They did not want to make the carpet worse. They wanted to make it better. They wanted to make Mom happy. They wanted to be good children.

Ben and Lily love to play baseball in the park. They have a big red ball and a small wooden bat. They take turns to hit the ball and run to the bases. They are very excited and happy.
One day, they hit the ball very hard and it flies over the fence. They run to the fence and look for the ball, but they cannot see it. They are sad and worried. They do not want to lose their ball.
"Where is our ball?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is in the bushes or under a car," Lily says.
They look around the fence, but they cannot find their ball. They are about to give up when they hear a voice.
"Hey, kids, are you looking for this?" the voice says.
They turn around and see a man holding their ball. He is smiling and friendly. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat with a star on it.
"Is this your ball?" he asks.
"Yes, it is! Thank you, mister!" Ben and Lily say.
They run to the man and take their ball. They are very excited and grateful. They hug the ball and hug the man.
"You're welcome, kids. I saw your ball land in my yard. It was a good hit. Do you like baseball?" the man asks.
"Yes, we do! We love baseball!" Ben and Lily say.
"Me too. I used to play baseball when I was young. Do you know who I am?" the man asks.
Ben and Lily look at the man and his hat. They see the star and the letters. They are surprised and amazed.
"Are you... are you a baseball star?" Ben asks.
The man nods and laughs.
"Yes, I am. I used to play for the Stars. My name is Joe. Do you want my autograph?" he asks.
Ben and Lily nod and smile.
"Yes, please!" they say.
The man takes a pen and writes his name on their ball. He gives it back to them and says:
"Here you go, kids. Keep playing and have fun. Maybe one day you will be baseball stars too."
Ben and Lily thank the man again and say goodbye. They run back to the park and continue to play baseball. They are very excited and proud. They have their ball and a new friend. They do not lose their ball. They find a baseball star.

"Mom, look what I found!" Tom said, holding up the rock. His mom looked at the rock and smiled. "That's a pretty rock, Tom. It has value," she said. Tom didn't know what "value" meant, but he liked how the rock looked.
Tom decided to keep the rock and show it to his friends. He put it in his pocket and went to the park. He showed the rock to his friends, and they all thought it was cool. They played with the rock and their toys all day, having lots of fun.
In the end, Tom learned that his light, shiny rock had value because it made him and his friends happy. And that was the best kind of value to have.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden after dinner. They liked to look at the stars and the moon in the sky. They saw a small light moving fast. It was a firefly.
"Look, Tom, a firefly!" Lily said. "It glows in the dark. It is so pretty."
"I want to catch it," Tom said. He ran after the firefly. He tried to grab it with his hand. But the firefly was too quick. It flew away.
"Be careful, Tom," Lily said. "Don't hurt the firefly. It is a living thing. It has feelings too."
Tom stopped running. He looked at Lily. He felt sorry. He did not want to hurt the firefly. He wanted to be its friend.
"Sorry, Lily," Tom said. "You are right. The firefly is a living thing. It has feelings too. I just wanted to see it closer."
Lily smiled. She had an idea. She took a glass jar from the porch. She put some grass and leaves in it. She made a hole in the lid.
"Let's try this," Lily said. "We can catch the firefly gently and put it in the jar. Then we can look at it for a while. But we have to let it go later. It needs to be free."
Tom nodded. He liked Lily's idea. He took the jar from Lily. They waited for the firefly to come near. They moved slowly and quietly. They caught the firefly and put it in the jar. They closed the lid.
They looked at the firefly in the jar. It glowed with a white light. It was so beautiful. They felt happy.
"Hello, firefly," Lily said. "We are Lily and Tom. We are your friends. We will not hurt you. We will let you go soon. Thank you for your light."
The firefly blinked its light. It seemed to say hello back. Lily and Tom smiled. They held the jar in their hands. They felt the firefly's warmth. They felt the firefly's life. They felt the firefly's glow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally was 3 years old, and she loved to play. One night, Sally lay down in her bed and wanted to go to sleep. But after she had closed her eyes, she could not fall asleep. She felt very troubled.
Sally's mom heard her daughter crying and came into the room. 
"What's wrong, Sally?" asked Mom.
"I can't sleep!" Sally said. 
Mom gave her daughter a hug. "It's ok," she said. "Try and take some slow deep breaths."
Sally took some deep breaths, and soon felt her eyelids getting really heavy. She closed her eyes again, and this time she felt herself drifting into a deep sleep.
The next morning, when Sally woke up, she felt like she had slept really well. She had a big smile on her face and she felt much better. 
Sally's teacher asked the class how they had slept the night before. When it was her turn to answer, Sally was able to proudly tell her teacher, "I had a good sleep and it made me happy!" 
The teacher smiled and replied, "That's wonderful, Sally. A good sleep helps us to be calm and focused in class as pupils." 
Sally felt proud of herself and was happy to have been able to solve her troubled sleep problem

Then one day he met a fox, and they had a long meeting. The fox said that the rabbit should never go exploring without asking anyone for help. The rabbit learned his lesson and thanked the fox.
But one day the rabbit decided to ignore the fox's advice and went exploring deep into the forest by himself. He got so lost that he could not find his way back home. He was feeling very scared and worried about his situation.
The rabbit suffered in the deep, dark, dangerous forest for many days. He was so weak and exhausted from all the walking and hunger.
Finally, when he had all but lost his courage, he got saved. The fox had come to rescue him, and the rabbit learned that he should never have listened to himself and should have listened to the fox's advice. He realised that sometimes it’s better to be safe than sorry.

Anna and Ben want to pass the pasta. But they see something outside. It is a big dog. The dog is black and white. It has a loud bark. The dog runs to the fence. It jumps on the fence. It tries to get in the yard.
Anna and Ben are alert. They are scared of the dog. They forget the pasta. They run to Mom. They say, "Mom, Mom, there is a big dog outside. It is scary. It wants to come in."
Mom goes to the window. She sees the dog. She is not scared. She knows the dog. She says, "That is Spot. He is our neighbor's dog. He is friendly. He likes to play. He does not want to hurt us. He just wants to say hello."
Mom opens the door. She calls Spot. Spot stops barking. He wags his tail. He comes to Mom. He licks her hand. He is happy. Mom pets Spot. She says, "Good boy, Spot. You are a nice dog. But you are too loud. You scared Anna and Ben. You should be quiet."
Mom takes Spot to the fence. She opens the gate. She says, "Go home, Spot. Go to your owner. He is looking for you. He misses you. He will give you a treat." Spot runs to his owner. He barks goodbye. He is happy.
Mom goes back to the table. She says, "Sorry, kids. That was Spot. He is not a bad dog. He is just a noisy dog. He likes to visit us. But he should not jump on the fence. He should stay in his yard. Now, let's eat our pasta. It is getting cold. Pass the pasta, please."
Anna and Ben pass the pasta. They are not scared anymore. They are hungry. They eat their pasta with cheese. They like it. They say, "Thank you, Mom. This is yummy pasta. We like pasta. And we like Spot. But we like him better when he is quiet."

Once upon a time, in a distant land, there lived a big, red hen. She loved to lay eggs for all her friends. The hen's friends would come from the east, west, north, and south to get her eggs. They loved her eggs because they were big and tasty.
One day, the hen laid a very special egg. It was shiny and golden. All her friends wanted the golden egg. They began to fight over who should have it. The hen was sad to see her friends fight.
Then, something unexpected happened. The shiny, golden egg began to crack. Out came a little, yellow chick. The chick looked at the fighting friends and said, "Please don't fight. Share and be kind to each other." The friends stopped fighting and felt sorry. They learned that being kind and sharing is more important than having the most special things.
From that day on, the friends never fought again. They shared everything and lived happily ever after. The hen continued to lay eggs, and the little, yellow chick grew up to be a wise and kind leader. The moral of the story is to always share and be kind to your friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, Lily has a cake. It is her birthday cake. It is big and pink and has candles on it.
Ben sees the cake. He wants some cake. He asks Lily, "Can I borrow some cake?"
Lily says, "No, you cannot borrow cake. Cake is not for borrowing. Cake is for eating. And this is my birthday cake. You can have some later, after we sing and blow the candles."
Ben is sad and angry. He thinks Lily is mean. He waits until Lily is not looking. Then he tries to take some cake. But he is not careful. He knocks the cake off the table. The cake falls on the floor. It is broken. The candles go out.
Lily hears the noise. She turns around. She sees the broken cake. She sees Ben. She is very upset. She cries, "Ben, what did you do? You broke my birthday cake! That was not nice. That was very bad. You are not my friend anymore."
Ben feels sorry. He did not mean to break the cake. He says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was hungry. I wanted some cake. I did not mean to break it. Please forgive me. Please be my friend again."
Lily stops crying. She looks at Ben. She sees that he is sorry. She says, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not borrow cake again. Cake is not for borrowing. Cake is for sharing. Do you understand?"
Ben nods. He says, "I understand, Lily. I promise. I will not borrow cake again. I will share cake with you. And I will help you clean up the mess."
Lily smiles. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are my friend again. Come on, let's clean up. Maybe we can still have some cake. And maybe we can make another wish."
They hug. They clean up. They have some cake. They make another wish. They are happy.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and clothes. One day, they find a big black hanger in their closet. They wonder what it is for.
"Look, Sam, a big black hanger!" Tim says. "What can we do with it?"
"Maybe we can hang our clothes on it," Sam says. "Or we can use it as a hook."
They try to hang their shirts on the hanger, but they are too small. The hanger is too big. They try to use it as a hook, but they cannot reach the ceiling. The hanger is too heavy.
"Let's weigh the hanger," Tim says. "Maybe it is very heavy."
They find a scale in the bathroom. They put the hanger on the scale. The scale shows a big number. They cannot read the number, but they know it is big.
"Wow, the hanger is very heavy!" Sam says. "It is heavier than our toys and clothes."
"Maybe it is not a hanger," Tim says. "Maybe it is something else."
They take the hanger back to their room. They look at it carefully. They see a small sticker on the hanger. It has some words and a picture. They cannot read the words, but they recognize the picture.
"Look, Sam, it is a picture of a bike!" Tim says. "The hanger is for a bike!"
"Maybe it is Dad's hanger," Sam says. "Maybe he uses it to hang his bike in the garage."
They decide to take the hanger to the garage. They find Dad's bike there. They try to hang the bike on the hanger, but they cannot lift it. The bike is too heavy.
"Dad, Dad, we found your hanger!" Tim says. "We tried to hang your bike on it, but we couldn't."
Dad comes to the garage. He sees the hanger and the bike. He smiles.
"Thank you, boys, for finding my hanger," Dad says. "It is a special hanger for my bike. It helps me save space in the garage. But you are right, it is very heavy. You need to be careful with it. Do you want to help me hang the bike on it?"
"Yes, Dad, we want to help!" Tim and Sam say.
Dad lifts the bike and puts it on the hanger. He shows Tim and Sam how to hook the hanger on the wall. The bike hangs on the hanger. It looks cool.
"Wow, Dad, your bike looks cool on the hanger!" Tim and Sam say.
"Thank you, boys, you are very helpful," Dad says. "Now, let's go inside and have some cookies. You deserve a treat for finding my hanger."
Tim and Sam are happy. They follow Dad to the kitchen. They have some cookies and milk. They tell Dad about their adventure with the big black hanger. Dad listens and laughs. He hugs them and tells them he loves them. They love him too. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She was very excited to go to the park and play on the swings. When she arrived, she saw a swing made of ice. She hopped on it and gave it a try. A few seconds later the swing broke, and Emily fell down onto the icy ground. 
Emily started to cry. A nearby boy noticed her and came over to help. He mentioned that it would be wise to stay off the icy swing. But Emily didn't listen and she kept playing on it.
So the boy decided to tell his father. His dad mentioned that this could be dangerous because the swing could break. But despite the warnings, Emily kept riding the swing and ignored her father.
Eventually, Emily's swing did break, and she fell hard onto the icy ground. She was very hurt and started crying. The boy, his father, and a nearby park ranger all rushed to Emily's aid. 
The park ranger noticed something strange. He mentioned that the swing should not have been made of ice. But now it was too late - Emily was already badly injured and had to be taken to the hospital. 
The moral of the story is to always listen to warnings. Emily knew better than to play on a swing made of ice, but she just didn't listen. Unfortunately, this disobedience caused her to get hurt in a very bad way.
